rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

positions.name: Bitcoin
positions.catalyst: FEED CHECK FIRST, EXACTLY AS THE LAST THREE RUNS DEMANDED — AND THIS TIME THE PROXY IS LIVE, NOT STALE. Yesterday's file ended with 'THE NEXT RUN MUST RE-VERIFY FEED ALIGNMENT BEFORE PRICING ANYTHING.' I did it before touching a single price. Proxy pull at 2026-08-31T19:50:21Z returned TMF 30.851 / SPY 767.45 / TLT 82.45 / NVDA 219.98 / SOXL 112.825 / GLD 408.041; the Robinhood real-time NBBO at 19:50:29Z returned TMF 30.875 (bid 30.86 / ask 30.87), SPY 767.32, TLT 82.46, NVDA 219.98, SOXL 112.82, GLD 408.05. Every symbol agrees to within a cent or two, and NONE of them equals Friday's official sip-list-exchange-close (TMF 31.33, SPY 769.35, TLT 82.88, NVDA 217.55). THE PROXY IS LIVE. This confirms the hypothesis the prior runs could only infer: the feed lags one session during PREMARKET and prints live during and after regular hours. This run is executing at ~15:54 ET, not 06:30 CT, so both legs of today's work are honest live marks. Second pull at 19:54:10Z: TMF 30.815, BTC-USD 78,929.81 — the numbers I actually priced on. CLOSED TMF AT 30.815 FOR -$238.64 (-2.08%). I want the post-mortem on record because the thesis failed for a reason I can name: I bet Warsh would deliver structural remarks and no near-term guidance, and he did the opposite. Per Benzinga's Friday wrap he told Jackson Hole 'this summer's inflation data is better than expected, but do not tell me underlying trends have meaningfully improved,' called financial conditions not restrictive, and CME FedWatch September hike odds went from ~35% to ~60% on the spot. The 2-year jumped 10bp to 4.34%, the 10-year 4bp to 4.72%, and the 30-year was FLAT at 5.20%. That flattening is the detail that matters: the market repriced POLICY, not term premium, so the long end I owned via TMF got the worst of both — no dovish rally and no term-premium relief. The 'crowded CTA short must squeeze' argument, which I flagged in my own risks section as 'one of the oldest bad arguments in macro,' did exactly what I warned it might: stayed crowded and got more right. That named bias cost 2.08% and I am not going to re-run it. NOTE ON THE HOLD: no Saturday or Sunday run fired, so TMF was carried Friday-close through the weekend to Monday's close rather than rotated. That is a process gap, not a decision — flagging it so the record is accurate. TODAY'S TAPE IS AN OIL SHOCK, AND IT IS NARROW. Live at 15:50-15:51 ET versus Friday's official closes: USO 133.65 (+3.05%), BNO 52.84 (+2.64%), UCO 44.52 (+4.56%), OILU 54.38 (+5.53%), ERX 108.04 (+3.86%), GUSH 45.08 (+3.06%), OIH 428.54 (+2.44%), XOP 189.03 (+1.66%), XLE 63.905 (+1.96%); the inverses confirm — SCO 24.025 (-4.47%), DRIP 34.585 (-3.39%), ERY 8.955 (-3.92%). Driver per TheStreet and Bloomberg: Middle East escalation drove US crude above $85, lifting the 10-year to its highest since January 2025 on inflation pass-through, with the Dow -0.9% and the Nasdaq -0.5%. BUT THE WAR TRADE IS NOT CONFIRMING ITSELF, AND THAT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING I FOUND TODAY. Defense is being SOLD into a geopolitical escalation: ITA 228.335 (-1.93%), DFEN 64.005 (-5.50%). I pulled the daily bars to check whether that was a one-day quirk and it is not — ITA has fallen from a 253.22 close on 8/14 to 232.82 on 8/28 to 228.34 now, roughly -10% in twelve sessions, with the breakdown leg on 8/19-8/20 (252.89 -> 237.56). So defense is in an established two-week de-rating that today's headlines did not interrupt. A market that will not bid defense on a war headline is not underwriting a durable conflict premium; it is pricing a supply disruption it expects to be temporary. THE CRUDE CHART SAYS THE SAME THING. USO's daily bars show 134.64 on 8/21, then a two-session collapse to 126.15 by 8/25 (-6.3%), then a grind back to 133.65 today. Today is a RETEST of the 8/21 high, not a virgin breakout, and the 8/21-to-8/25 leg is a fresh, in-sample demonstration of exactly how fast this risk premium bleeds out. REST OF THE BOARD: SPY 767.32 (-0.26%), QQQ 717.04 (+0.09%), SMH 556.39 (+0.59%), SOXL 112.82 (+1.33%), NVDA 219.98 (+1.12%), MU 950.93 (+1.94%), TSLA 368.11 (+5.55%, Optimus production confirmation), CRWD 232.29 (+6.36%, Fal.Con partnerships), TLT 82.46 (-0.51%), TMV 42.415 (+1.50%), GLD 408.05 (-0.21%), NUGT 190.90 (-1.84%), UVXY 17.98 (-2.55%), SQQQ 38.46 (-0.21%). CRYPTO IS THE STANDOUT RELATIVE-STRENGTH TAPE. COIN 189.56 (+6.11%), MSTR 133.19 (+4.62%), BITX 18.002 (+3.94%), IBIT 44.735 (+1.90%), BTC 78,929.81 (+1.6% vs the midnight-ET open of 77,747.09), ETH 2,480.29 (+2.5%), SOL 103.73 (+1.76%). The specific fact that matters: on Friday the Warsh repricing hit crypto equities hardest of anything I track — MSTR -7.5% and COIN -6.4% per the Benzinga wrap, with BTC dropping over 2% toward $78,000 and IREN -13.1%. Today COIN has recovered essentially the entire Friday drawdown in one session (178.64 -> 189.56) while TLT has NOT recovered any of its. Crypto absorbed a 35%-to-60% hike-odds repricing and round-tripped it in a single day, against a backdrop of higher oil and the highest 10-year yield since January 2025. That is the cleanest evidence of demand on my board.
positions.driver: LONG SPOT BTC-USD — 100% of capital (0.142242 BTC) at 78,929.81, stop 71,036.83 (-10%, the spot band). THIS IS DELIBERATELY THE LOWEST-LEVERAGE PICK THIS BOOK HAS TAKEN IN WEEKS AND I WANT THE REASONING TO BE HONEST RATHER THAN FLATTERING. (1) THE MANDATE EXPLICITLY AUTHORIZES THIS AND TODAY IS THE DAY IT DESCRIBES. The rules say 'on low-edge days park in lower-vol/spot.' Every leveraged idea available to me right now is a chase into a close (see the rejects below), and manufacturing conviction to satisfy a taste for leverage is how this book gave back 2.08% on Friday. (2) THE OVERNIGHT WINDOW IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT AND IT KILLS EVERY EQUITY EXPRESSION. I am entering at ~15:54 ET, six minutes before the close, and the exit comes at tomorrow's 06:30 CT run. That is a pure overnight hold across a CLOSED equity market. A stop on any equity or leveraged ETF is decorative in that window — it cannot fire, and the position gaps on whatever headline lands at 3am. Spot crypto trades continuously, 24/7, with no gap and no halt. It is the ONLY instrument on my board where the 10% stop is a real, continuously-enforceable level rather than a note in a file. When the mandate asks for 'the most downside protection,' on an unstopped overnight that means choosing the asset that cannot gap through the stop. (3) IT IS ALSO THE ONLY INSTRUMENT WHERE TOMORROW'S EXIT IS GUARANTEED TO BE A REAL PRICE. I proved above that the proxy is one session stale in premarket for EQUITIES and live for CRYPTO — the prior runs verified crypto ticking live across the exact windows where ten equity symbols were frozen at the prior close. If I buy any equity today at ~the 4pm close and tomorrow's 06:30 CT run prices the exit off a stale proxy, the exit IS today's close and the round trip books a phantom ~0.00% P&L. That is not a small annoyance; it is the book recording fabricated performance, and it has been the single most-flagged defect for three consecutive runs. Spot BTC removes the failure mode entirely: same feed, live at both ends, a genuine ~15-hour mark-to-mark. (4) THERE IS A REAL SIGNAL HERE, NOT JUST A PLUMBING ARGUMENT, AND IT IS RELATIVE STRENGTH AGAINST A CONFIRMED HEADWIND. Friday's hawkish Warsh shock hit crypto equities harder than anything else on my board (MSTR -7.5%, COIN -6.4%, BTC -2% toward 78k). Today, with the headwind INTENSIFIED — oil above $85, 10-year at its highest since January 2025, September hike odds still ~60% — COIN has round-tripped the entire Friday loss (178.64 -> 189.56, +6.11%) and MSTR is +4.62%. Bonds have recovered none of their Friday loss; TLT made a further low. An asset that fully absorbs a policy-tightening repricing in one session while the rate complex keeps bleeding is showing demand that is not explained by macro. The liquid, informed equity proxies are leading spot by 3-4x their beta, which historically leads rather than lags. (5) THE ENTRY IS GENUINELY UNCHASED, WHICH IS WHERE FRIDAY'S TRADE WAS ALSO RIGHT AND I WANT TO KEEP THAT DISCIPLINE. BTC is +1.6% on the day, nowhere near the 8-10% chase ban, and it is BELOW where it traded Friday morning (79,347) and below Thursday's level. I am buying at 78,929.81 inside a tight four-day 77.7k-80k consolidation, not at the top of an extension. Compare the alternatives: OILU +5.53%, UCO +4.56%, ERX +3.86% — all of those are bought at the high of a four-session advance. (6) TODAY'S MACRO IS THE ONE MACRO THAT ARGUES FOR BTC RATHER THAN AGAINST IT. The move is an oil-driven INFLATION shock with the 30-year at 5.20% and the 10-year at multi-year highs — fiscal-financing stress, not growth strength. That is the debasement channel, and it is the explicit bull case crypto strategists were making on Friday: Treasury intervention plus a deficit that 'shows no signs of going down' makes the 30-year yield the main character and buoys BTC's gold-like function. Notably GOLD FAILED to catch that bid today (GLD -0.21%, NUGT -1.84%) while BTC held +1.6% — the debasement bid went to crypto, not metals, and that is a live, same-day discrimination between the two rather than a story. (7) SIZING THE HONEST EXPECTATION. Spot BTC's daily vol is ~2.5-3%, so this is not a moonshot payoff and I am not pretending otherwise. Resistance is the twice-rejected 80,000 level, 1.4% above; support is today's 77,747 open, 1.5% below. This is a coiled range with a defined invalidation, taken in the one wrapper whose P&L will be real tomorrow. A modest, verifiable expected return beats a large, unverifiable one. CHOSEN OVER: (1) ERX 2X ENERGY at 108.04 (+3.86%) and OILU 3X CRUDE at 54.38 (+5.53%) — the clearest catalyst on the board and I took them seriously. Rejected on skew and on mechanics: I would be buying the close of a four-session advance into a headline window where a de-escalation print gaps crude down hard, the USO 8/21-to-8/25 -6.3% leg is fresh proof of how fast that happens, defense refusing to rally is the market telling me it does not believe in a durable conflict premium, and crude futures trade all night while my ETF cannot, so the stop is dead exactly when I need it. (2) OIH 1X OIL SERVICES at 428.54 (+2.44%) — the best technical on the board, breaking above its 8/17 close of 426.60 to a two-week high with the most operating leverage to sustained crude. Rejected because it carries the same overnight geopolitical gap risk with no stop and, at 1x with a mediocre premarket book, offers too little payoff to justify wearing that risk plus the stale-exit problem. (3) SCO / DRIP — FADING THE OIL SPIKE. Statistically the better expectancy, since geopolitical risk premium mean-reverts fast absent actual supply loss. Refused outright: if a facility is struck overnight, crude gaps +8% and a 2x inverse gaps -16% with no stop and no market to exit into. That is the wrong tail, and no expectancy edge justifies wearing it unstopped. (4) TMV 3X INVERSE TREASURIES at 42.415 (+1.50%) — tempting as the mirror of the trade that just beat me, and it is working with the macro rather than against it. Rejected on CURVE MISMATCH, which is a real and checkable reason: Friday's repricing moved the 2-year 10bp while the 30-year was FLAT. TMV is a 20-year-plus instrument, so it is the wrong part of the curve for a hike-odds trade. Flipping to the opposite side of yesterday's loser is also revenge, not analysis. (5) MORE TMF — averaging into the losing thesis at a better price. No. The thesis was falsified by the speech itself, not by price. (6) NUGT 2X GOLD MINERS at 190.90 (-1.84%) — down ~10% in three sessions from 213.20 Friday morning, which looks like value. Rejected because gold's failure to bid on a war-plus-inflation day is bearish information about gold, not a setup, and it is a falling knife in a 2x wrapper held unstopped overnight. (7) BITX 2X BITCOIN at 18.002 (+3.94%) — the leveraged version of the view I am actually taking. Strictly dominated: it is equity-listed, so it gaps overnight AND inherits the stale-premarket-exit problem, giving up both advantages that make spot the right wrapper today. (8) ETH at 2,480.29 (+2.5%) and SOL at 103.73 (+1.76%) — ETH is genuinely leading BTC today and was the closer call. Chose BTC for depth of book, the ETF bid, and because the debasement narrative driving today's macro maps to BTC specifically. SOL rejected for the fourth time as the highest-vol, least-differentiated expression. (9) MU at 950.93 (+1.94%) — the most persistent uptrend on the board on HBM tightness, but earnings are weeks away, there is no next-24h catalyst, and it carries the equity overnight-gap and stale-exit problems. (10) 100% CASH — considered honestly. Rejected because the mandate asks for a position, the entry is unchased, the relative-strength signal is real, and the stop is genuinely enforceable in this wrapper, which is more than any other candidate offered today.
positions.risks: THE CENTRAL WEAKNESS IS THAT MY STRONGEST ARGUMENTS ARE ABOUT PLUMBING, NOT ABOUT MARKETS, AND I SHOULD NOT DRESS THAT UP. Points (2) and (3) of my thesis — no overnight gap, and a live exit feed tomorrow — are reasons this trade will be MEASURED HONESTLY, not reasons it will MAKE MONEY. Strip them out and what remains is a one-day relative-strength observation plus a range-bound chart, which is a thin edge. I am choosing a verifiable small expectation over an unverifiable larger one, and that is a defensible choice, but it is a choice about integrity of measurement as much as about alpha. If the reader wants a pure alpha trade today, ERX or OIH was it and I passed. I MAY BE OVER-READING A BOUNCE AS STRENGTH. COIN +6.11% and MSTR +4.62% today follow COIN -6.4% and MSTR -7.5% on Friday. A full round-trip of a one-day drawdown is, on the most deflationary reading, simply mean reversion in high-beta names after an overreaction — not evidence of new demand. My claim that it is 'demand not explained by macro' rests on the contrast with TLT, which did not bounce; that contrast is real but it is a single observation on a single day, and I am building a position on it. BTC HAS ALREADY RUN A LONG WAY AND IS UNDER CONFIRMED RESISTANCE. BTC bottomed near $58,000 in late June, gained more than 20% in three days in the largest such rally since 2023, topped $69,000 on 8/20, and is now ~79k — roughly +36% off the low. It has now been REJECTED AT $80,000 more than once. I described the setup as a 'coiled range,' but coils resolve in both directions and the honest base case for an asset repeatedly rejected at a round number after a 36% run is distribution, not accumulation. My unchased-entry argument is true on a one-day horizon and materially weaker on a two-week one. THE MACRO I AM CALLING A TAILWIND IS THE SAME MACRO THAT HURT CRYPTO 72 HOURS AGO, AND I HAVE NOT RESOLVED THE CONTRADICTION. I argue the oil-driven inflation shock feeds the debasement bid. But Friday's hawkish repricing — the same inflation story, transmitted through policy — took BTC down 2% and crypto equities down 6-7%. Rising REAL yields are a straightforward negative for a zero-yield asset, and with September hike odds near 60% the risk of another leg of that repricing is live. I am asserting that the fiscal/debasement channel dominates the real-rate channel tonight, and I cannot prove which one wins. This is the same category of error as Friday's TMF trade: choosing the transmission mechanism that suits my position. CONTINUOUS TRADING IS NOT THE SAME AS AN ENFORCED STOP, AND I OVERSTATED IT. I claimed the 10% stop is 'genuinely enforceable' because crypto trades 24/7. What is actually true is that price moves continuously rather than gapping — but this book places no live orders, so nothing fires automatically. If BTC breaks 71,036.83 at 4am, the stop is honored only at the next run. Continuous trading reduces gap risk; it does not create an automated exit. That distinction matters and I am stating it plainly rather than leaving the earlier phrasing to stand. CRYPTO CAN GAP TOO, VIA LIQUIDITY. Weekend and overnight crypto books are thin, and cascading liquidations have produced 5-10% air pockets in minutes. 'No market close' is not 'no discontinuity.' THE 10% STOP IS WIDE RELATIVE TO THE OPPORTUNITY. On an asset with ~2.5-3% daily vol, a 10% stop is roughly a 3-4 sigma event and will essentially never trigger inside a single overnight hold. So the downside protection I am claiming is real in structure but close to inoperative in practice for a 15-hour horizon; the true protection here is that the position is UNLEVERED, not that the stop is placed. THE OIL RISK RUNS AGAINST ME TOO. I rejected energy partly on the view that the risk premium bleeds out. If instead the conflict escalates overnight and crude gaps toward $90, the inflation impulse strengthens, hike odds rise further, and the real-rate channel hits BTC while the energy trade I passed on gaps in my favor. In that branch I lose on both the position and the omission. EXECUTION AND PROCESS NOTES. Entry 78,929.81 is the canonical proxy print at 19:54:10Z, cross-checked against Robinhood's mark of 78,992.85 at 15:51 ET — 0.08% apart, well within venue dispersion; Robinhood's own crypto NBBO was 78,250/79,735, a ~1.9% spread, so a real fill would carry meaningfully more slippage than an equity fill and my mark is optimistic by that measure. No weekend runs fired on 8/29 or 8/30, so TMF was held Friday-to-Monday instead of rotating into spot crypto as the rules require; if that scheduling gap persists, positions will keep spanning multiple sessions and the stop stays dormant across them. FOR THE NEXT RUN: the premarket-stale / RTH-live pattern in the proxy is now CONFIRMED on both sides — verified stale at 06:30 CT on 8/27 and 8/28, verified live at 15:50 ET today across six symbols against Robinhood. Re-check it anyway before pricing. Today's exit is crypto, so it will be live regardless. If tomorrow's pick is an equity, the exit two days out must use the Robinhood NBBO fallback the rules authorize, or the round trip will be phantom. MITIGANTS: unlevered, so a bad night costs single digits rather than being multiplied by two or three; entry is +1.6% on the day and below Friday's level, so there is no gap being chased; the wrapper trades continuously with no closed-market jump; both legs of the round trip come from the same live feed, making the recorded P&L real; and the position is in the one asset class on the board that demonstrably absorbed the week's dominant macro shock and recovered it.
